t: Nga pyrkhat lada phi lah ban [verb]
ex: Nga pyrkhat lada phi lah ban ïarap khyndiat ïa nga ha kane.
n: pyrkhat lada (think whether) is the soft written request; in speech Lada lah, sngewbha ... does the same job.

ex: Phi lah ban khang ïa ka window, sngewbha?
n: No 'mind' verb for requests: the polite frame is lah ban (can) as a question plus sngewbha.

ex: Phim sngewsih lada nga plie ïa ka window?
n: Literally 'won't you feel bad if I ...'. Yes-go-ahead is Em, wat sngewsih (no, don't feel bad).

ex: Nga dang pyrkhat ban leit shong ha Berlin u snem ba wan.
Nga kyrmen shibun ban ïohi biang ïa phi.
n: No fixed 'look forward to': kyrmen (hope) plus shibun, said warmly, carries the anticipation.

ex: Ngam tip shisha lada ki wan mynta ka miet ne em.
n: lada doubles as 'whether'; ne em (or not) at the end is common.

t: Nga dang kwah ban [verb] mynta hi
ex: Ah, nga dang kwah ban phone ïa phi mynta hi!
n: No fixed 'about to'; dang kwah (was just wanting) plus mynta hi (right now) is the everyday way.

t: Nga dang thmu ban [verb] naduh bun ka por
ex: Nga dang thmu ban phone ïa phi naduh bun ki taiew.
n: dang plus naduh keeps the intention open; the English perfect needs no la here.

t: Ym don jingmyntoi ban [verb] / Ym donkam ban [verb]
ex: Ym don jingmyntoi ban ap, kim wan.
n: jingmyntoi is benefit; ym donkam ban (no need to) is the lighter everyday form.

ex: Kumno lada ngin thied ka pizza mynta ka miet?
Nga kham kwah ban sah ha ïing mynta ka miet, lada phim sngewsih.
n: kham (more) before kwah makes the preference; no conditional form is needed.

ex: Lada nga long phi, ngan kren bad u bah jong phi shwa.
n: To elders the softer ha ka jaka jong phi (in your place) is more natural.

ex: Ka ïadei hi bad ka suiñbneng.
n: hi after ïadei adds 'really, it just'.

t: Ka kam ka long, [clause] / Ka daw ka long ba [clause]
ex: Ka kam ka long, nga la lah don jingthmu ha ka sngi Saturday.
Map ïa nga, ngam shym la kwah ban kren hapdeng.
n: Literally 'I did not want to'; kren hapdeng (speak in the middle) is interrupt.

ex: Nga la nang ban ïeng shwa.
n: nang is both learn and get used to; dang nang ban is 'getting used to'.

ex: Ka shim kumba arphew minit ban poi hangta.
n: ka is the dummy subject; kumba before a number is 'about'.

ex: Sngewbha ïathuh ïa nga lada phi donkam eiei.
Khublei ba phi la ïathuh ïa nga.
n: ba plus a full clause does the work of English -ing; na ka bynta (for) takes a noun.

t: Map ïa nga ba nga la [verb]
ex: Map ïa nga ba nga la pynap ïa phi.
n: pynap is causative pyn- plus ap (wait): make someone wait.

ex: Ngam lah ban ngeit ba u la poi u bnai October.

t: Phi lah ban ïathuh ïa nga [clause]?
ex: Phi lah ban ïathuh ïa nga hangno ka steshon, sngewbha?
n: The embedded question keeps normal order; nothing inverts.

ex: Phi pyrkhat kumno shaphang ka ophis thymmai?
n: Khasi asks 'how do you think', not 'what'; aiu is wrong here.

ex: Kumno ka long ban shong ha London?
Map, hynrei ki kamra baroh ki la dap mynta ka miet.
Kynmaw ban khang bha ïa ka jingkhang haba phi mih.
n: kynmaw is remember; the bare imperative is fine here, sngewbha makes it softer.

ex: Nga kwah shibun, hynrei nga hap ban leit kam kham shwa lashai.
n: Refusals keep a reason; namar ba often follows.

ex: Ka la paw ba ka dukan ka la khang shi taiew baroh.
n: paw is appear, come to light; ka is the dummy subject.

ex: Ka ïthuh kumba kan slap.
Ngam tip ei ei ruh hangno nga la buh ïa ki chabi.
n: ei ei ruh (anything at all) is the emphatic blank; plain ngam tip is milder.

ex: Nga dei ban poi ha ophis ha khyndai baje.
n: dei ban covers must, should and supposed to; context decides the strength.

ex: Nga shu kwah ban kylli lada phi la ïoh ïa ka email jong nga.
n: shu (just, merely) is the softener.

ex: Ym don eiei hangno ngin bam. Ka long ha phi.
Kata ka bha shibun! Katno baje ngan wan?
n: No 'sound' verb: Khasi reacts with 'that is ...'. Bha, kumta accepts a plan.

ex: Nga hi nga la lah ban pynkhreh ïa ka printer.
n: la lah ban is plain past ability; nga hi (I myself) adds the effort.

ex: Ngi dei ban shim ka jingpyrkhat haduh ka sngi Friday.
To ngi shongthiah khyndiat bad dih ka kophi.
Phi lah ban peit khyndiat ïa ka laptop jong nga? Ka ju kam trei bha.
Ka dud ka la lut biang.
n: The supply is the subject: lut is 'be used up'. ngim don shuh (we have no more) also works.

ex: Ngan phone ïa u trai ïing lashai.
n: No single 'get in touch': say the actual contact (phone, kren, phah email).

ex: Map, nga la leh bakla ha ka booking.
Ngam shym la peit bha ïa ka por.

t: ka don jingmut / ka ïoh jingmut
ex: Kata kam don jingmut ïa nga.
n: Everyday speech often just says ngam sngewthuh (I don't get it).

ex: Me lah ban ïarap khyndiat ïa nga? Ai jingbam ïa ka miaw.
n: No 'favour' idiom; ïarap (help) plus khyndiat does it. Use pha to a woman.

ex: Me lah ban ïarap ïa nga ban kit kine ki box?
U pyrshang khlaiñ shisha ban nang ka ktien German.
Ka la shem ïa ka jingpyrkhat kaba bha shibun.
n: shem (find) covers 'come up with'.

ex: Nga donkam ban bred noh katto katne ki jaiñ barim.
n: bred noh is throw away; ai noh (give away) is the kinder option.

ex: Nga ïadei bha bad ki para nongtrei jong nga.
n: para nongtrei is colleague (fellow worker).

ex: Lada phi kylla ka jingpyrkhat, tang phone ïa nga.
Me lah ban peit ïa ka bag jong nga shi minit?
Ym don jingkloi, leh suki.
n: kloi is hurry; the idea is 'don't hurry, go slowly'.

ex: Nga pynlut bun ka por ha lynti ban leit sha kam.
n: pynlut is spend or use up (time, money).

ex: Ngam lah ban sngewthuh ïa kane ka app thymmai.
Nga dei ban pynbeit ïa ka visa jong nga kane ka taiew.
n: pynbeit (make straight) covers sort out, correct, settle.

ex: Ngan sa peit ïa kata lashai.
Map, ngam lah ban wan mynta ka miet.
n: No idiom: Khasi simply says 'can't come'.

ex: Ha kine ki sngi nga don jingeh ban thiah.
Map, nga dang wan lait khyndiat.
Nga dang shu buh sha hadien ban phone ïa u doktor bniat.
n: No fixed 'put off': buh sha hadien (put to later) is the plain way to say it.

ex: Ngin lah ban buh ka meeting ha ka taiew ba wan?
Nga la ïeh ban dih duma u snem ba la leit.
n: ïeh is leave, quit; dih duma is smoke.

ex: Ka jingthiah bha ka pynkylla shibun.
Phi lah ban sumar ïa ki khun ha ka sngi Saturday?
Ngam shym la ïoh lad ban phone biang ïa phi.
n: lad is way, opportunity; the negative past needs shym.

ex: Ban kren shisha, ngam shym la sngewtynnad eh ïa ka phlim.
Ap khyndiat, nga pyrkhat... ka la long ka sngi Tuesday ba la leit.
U long... kumno ban ong? U briew uba khlaiñ eh.

t: Me sngewthuh? / Phi sngewthuh ïa kaba nga ong?
ex: Kam long kumjuh shuh, me sngewthuh?
n: kumjuh is 'the same'. Rising tone does the work of the tag.

ex: Kat ba nga tip, ka meeting ka dang don.
Bad ruh, phi la sngew shaphang u Tom?
n: No fixed Khasi 'by the way'; Shillong speakers often just say it in English.

t: Kumno kumno ruh, kumba nga dang ong ...
ex: Kumno kumno ruh, kumba nga dang ong, ka hotel ka bha shibun.
Kata ka pynkynmaw ïa nga, nga dei ban phone ïa ka kmie.
n: pynkynmaw is the causative of kynmaw (remember).

ex: Nga sngewthuh ïa phi, hynrei nga dang pyrkhat ba ka jrong eh.
Ka dei, ngan leh kumjuh lada nga long me.
Ap khyndiat, ngan sa shim ka pen.
Ka la bha. Nga mut, ym kaba kyrduh eh, hynrei ka bha.
n: mut is 'mean'; ka mut ba (it means that) is the fuller form.

ex: Ha ka jingpeit jong nga, ka long tang ka jingpynlut pisa.
Hmm, ngam tip shisha shaphang kata.
Em, ha ka jingshisha, ka long kumta pat.
n: jingshisha is truth; the correction stays gentle with phi.

ex: Ym don eiei, ngan leh nga hi.
n: Same phrase as 'no worries'; tone decides.

ex: Ym don eiei, ka jia ïa baroh.
Bha, sa ïakynduh ka taiew ba wan. Shong suk!
n: The one leaving says shong suk, the one staying says leit suk.

ex: Wat sheptieng, kam dei kaba heh.
n: Literally 'it is not a big thing'; ym don eiei also works.

ex: Nga lah ban shim ka phone jong phi? — Hooid, shim noh.
n: noh makes the go-ahead casual; to a senior add sngewbha.

ex: Lashai nga don ka interview, kumta kyrmen ba kan long bha.
n: No gesture idiom; Khasi says 'hope it goes well'.

ex: Buh noh ïa ka pisa jong me, nga siew.
n: siew is pay; me to a man, pha to a woman.

ex: Khublei, ngan sa pyrkhat.
n: sa (later) makes it a soft, noncommittal answer.

ex: Phim lah ban wan? Sngewsih shibun!

t: La jngai ngim shym la ïakynduh!
ex: Hei, la jngai ngim shym la ïakynduh! Kumno me?
n: No fixed idiom; 'it's been long since we met' is what Shillong speakers say.

ex: Ka jrong. Ha kawei pat ka liang, kan sah bun snem.
Ka hotel ka barim khyndiat. Wat la kumta, ki nongtrei ki bha shibun.
Phim thngan? Lada kumta, te to ngi dih tang ka kophi.
n: te (then) pins the consequence.

ex: Phi lah ban shim tang lada phi pynphai biang.
Ngi la mih wat la ka slap.
Ki rel ki la ïeng. Namarkata nga la wan lait.
n: ïeng (stand still) is used for a strike stoppage; kumta is the lighter link.

ex: Ngan phone ïa phi tang ynda nga poi ha ïing.
n: tang ynda (only once) gives 'as soon as'.

ex: Ngi la ïakren bun ki kynta, hynrei ha kaba kut ngi la sah ha ïing.
Ai ïa u ban thiah. U la trei lut ka miet hi.
n: No fixed 'after all': hi (indeed) on the reason does the job.

ex: Shim ka syrbaïn, lehse kan slap.
n: No 'in case' conjunction: state the precaution, then lehse plus the risk.
